# Store a new item with its quantity

## Context
Story #3: adding a new item stores it with its quantity and unit.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `pantry add rice 2kg` on an empty store stores rice at 2kg.
- [ ] `pantry add rice 1kg` after it leaves rice at 3kg.

## Verify end to end
`pantry add rice 2kg && pantry add rice 1kg && pantry list` prints `rice 3kg`.

# Add an item

As a cook, I add an item with a quantity, so the pantry knows I have it.

## Rules
- Adding an item that exists adds to its quantity; the units must match.

## Examples
- `pantry add rice 2kg` then `pantry add rice 1kg` leaves rice at 3kg.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Adding a new item stores it with its quantity and unit.
- [ ] Adding to an existing item in another unit is refused with a message.

# Use some of an item

As a cook, I use some of an item, so the quantity goes down.

## Rules
- Using more than there is leaves zero and says so.

## Examples
- rice at 2kg, `pantry use rice 500g` leaves 1.5kg.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Using part of an item lowers its quantity.
- [ ] Using more than there is leaves zero and prints a warning.
